**FINDING (separate): skip:memory-gate label is NOT wired in governance.yml — ADR-0014 mentions it, YAML doesn't implement**

What: Registered as a SEPARATE finding from the #9 cutover blocker (human ruling: "registralo como hallazgo aparte"). The `memory-gate` job in .github/workflows/governance.yml (lines ~142-149) has NO `if:` / label guard — so a `skip:memory-gate` escape hatch does NOT exist, even though ADR-0014 references it. It is the sibling of the previously-found non-existent decision-gate skip label.

Why it matters: There is no sanctioned way to bypass the memory-gate on a PR that legitimately shouldn't carry a session summary — the only escape is an ad-hoc bypass, which the rung-1/no-bypass doctrine forbids. Contrast: the diff-size gate DOES implement its escape (`size:exception` check at governance.yml ~line 102).

Where: .github/workflows/governance.yml (memory-gate job, ~L142-149 — no conditional). ADR-0014 (mentions the label). 

Status: NOT fixed in the transitional records-aware micro-slice (out of scope, explicitly). Candidate for its own approved issue: wire `skip:memory-gate` as a label-gated `if:` on the memory-gate job, symmetric to `size:exception`, with the label itself governed (who can apply it).

Learned: This is doctrine↔implementation drift #N — an ADR names an affordance the YAML never grew. Same class as the earlier non-existent decision label finding.
